# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

I found no blockers and recommend merging. `cargo test` passes (127 passed, 0 failed), and so does the wasm release build. I did not run the grader, as instructed.

**The five items from the previous review:**
- **Re-grade:** the results are recorded in the new NOTES.md entry: goodboy video 0.081 to 1.0, goodboy audio 0.951 to 0.916, overall 0.7980 to 0.8476, mgba-dma and every other test unchanged, and nba-hw dma-start-delay (ungraded) 17 to 15 of 20. I could not check these numbers myself because I didn't run the grader.
- **gbatek quote:** it is correct. `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval/spec/gbatek.htm:2338` says "After changing the Enable bit from 0 to 1, wait 2 clock cycles before accessing any DMA related registers." The comment at `src/dma.rs:155` quotes that accurately and no longer claims the CPU keeps running for 2 cycles.
- **NOTES.md entry:** added. It also marks the Phase 2 one-step delay as superseded, records that the integrator edited `src/dma.rs` because it has no Phase 5 owner, and adds a row for the goodboy agent.
- **Stale test helper:** `run_after_start_delay` is removed, and all of its callers now call `run_pending_transfers` once. The `start_delay_steps` field is gone too; nothing else in the code still refers to it.
- **Enable-then-cancel test:** added as `immediate_transfer_runs_before_the_next_instruction_can_cancel_it`. It does catch the old bug: with the one-step delay, the first call only used up the delay and the disabling write would have cancelled the copy.

**Correctness:** the transfer now starts right after the enabling instruction. Enabling a channel sets `pending`, and `src/gba.rs:59` runs pending transfers after every `cpu.step`, so the copy happens before the next instruction can disable it. Disabling still clears `pending` (`write_control`, `src/dma.rs:167`). gbatek only tells software to wait, so making the start immediate is allowed, and the remaining timing gap is noted in a `ponytail:` comment.

**Originality:** clean. The comment cites only gbatek and the measured behaviour of a ROM, and nothing branches on a ROM.

**Findings:**
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/dma.rs:416`: [minor] The new test writes the control value as the magic number `0x8400` with a trailing comment, while the other tests in the module use `ENABLE_BIT | WORD_SIZE_BIT`. Suggested fix: use the named constants.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/NOTES.md:78`: [minor] The goodboy audio score dropped from 0.951 to 0.916. The entry records the drop but gives no reason, and it is a fall in a graded score. Suggested fix: add one clause on the likely cause, or flag it for a later Phase 5 round.
